summary: Flux is an archived architecture library, and the library is the smallest part of it. src holds fourteen files: a Dispatcher, two store base classes, a React container and a legacy mixin. Around that sit 106 files of worked examples, a Docusaurus site, translated docs and a checked-in dist build. Archived in March 2023.

importantModules.role: The whole idea in one file: registered callbacks, single dispatch, and waitFor to order store updates.
The store base class: registers with a dispatcher, tracks change state and emits to subscribers.
A store defined as a reduce over actions, the shape most later state libraries adopted.
Wraps a React component so it re-renders when the stores it declares change.
The bookkeeping behind a container: swaps listeners when the store list changes and groups them so state is recalculated once per dispatch.
Registers one callback that waits for every store in a group, so a listener fires once per dispatch after all of them have updated.
The pre-container mixin API, kept for components written before FluxContainer existed.
One helper the store classes share: raises an invariant naming the method a subclass was supposed to override.
The flux/utils entry point: re-exports Container, Mixin, ReduceStore and Store from the compiled lib directory.
The package main, which exports only Dispatcher from the compiled lib directory; the store classes come from flux/utils instead.
Version 4.0.4, depending only on fbemitter and fbjs with React as a peer; build runs gulp and test runs jest.
Pins the dispatcher contract: waitFor in both registration orders, dispatch while dispatching, circular waits and unregister.
Test setup: runs only src, resolves the flat module names the sources import, transforms through the local preprocessor and uses jsdom.
Compiles each file through babel with the shared default options before Jest runs it.
The babel-preset-fbjs settings shared by build and tests: rewrites module names such as invariant and strips __DEV__ code.
Sets the global __DEV__ flag to true so the development-only invariants run during tests.
The build: babel-compiles src into lib, then webpacks index.js and utils.js into UMD bundles in dist with a version header.
Release notes from 2.1.0 to 4.0.3, including the FluxMapStore removal in 3.0.0 and the fbjs 3.0.1 upgrade that closed CVE-2021-27292.
The long-form explanation of the architecture: actions, dispatcher, stores and views arranged as a unidirectional cycle.
The dispatcher reference: how it differs from pub-sub, plus register, unregister, waitFor, dispatch and isDispatching.
Reference for the three classes in flux/utils, Store, ReduceStore and Container, stated as a starting point rather than a framework.
The reading order for the examples, from concepts through TodoMVC, testing, Flow and the async application.
The tutorial itself: six numbered steps that build TodoMVC from the flux-shell starter, adding dispatcher, actions, store, container and views in turn.
The example's Express backend: todos in a JSON file, a forced 250-2000ms delay and a 25% error rate, so the client has to cope with slow, failing calls.
The code-free introduction to dispatcher, store, action and view, and why the data flow only goes one way.
Configuration for the published documentation site, including the banner announcing that the project is archived.
Contribution rules: branch from master, complete the Facebook CLA, and follow the code conventions of semicolons, two-space indent and 80-column lines.
The landing page, which opens with the archive notice pointing readers at Redux, MobX, Recoil, Zustand or Jotai.

strengths: The library is small enough to read completely: the dispatcher is one file and the store hierarchy is four.
Every concept in the documentation has a matching runnable example, which is why the pattern spread as far as it did.
Tests sit in __tests__ directories beside the modules they cover, one per class.
The documentation explains an architecture rather than an API, and it survives independently of this code.
concerns: The repository is archived and was last pushed in March 2023; the project is finished, not paused.
Examples outweigh the library by roughly seven to one, so the repository size says nothing about the code you would depend on.
Built bundles are committed under dist, so the repository carries generated output next to its source.
The Korean translations cover only part of the documentation, and nothing keeps them in step with the English originals.
FluxMixinLegacy is a second, older way to do the same thing, retained inside a library this small.
